Subject: Private Offer pricing & term questions for Redwood Inference

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the latency/throughput numbers look promising for our clinical summarization workload. Our procurement team asked for a couple of clarifications before we move to PO:

1) We prefer a 12-month committed term. Can you confirm whether Redwood can offer a yearly committed private offer (AWS PO) vs a purely usage-based listing, and what the modeled cost delta looks like?
2) Our finance threshold requires that any private offer above $150k/year be reviewed by CFO and legal. What approvals do you typically see on your side for multi-year/enterprise discounts?
3) We also need to know whether co-sell incentives change pricing or require additional paperwork on the buyer side.

Attached are our standard procurement questions — happy to hop on a call.

Best,

Clearwave Health

Subject: Re: Private Offer pricing & term questions for Redwood Inference

Aisha — thanks for the thoughtful list and for sharing the doc. Short answers up front, full details below and a proposed next step.

TL;DR:
- We can support either a 12-month committed private offer (reserved capacity or committed usage) or a usage-first private offer.
- Yearly committed usually yields a 10–30% unit discount vs on-demand usage depending on commit level and whether you select Dedicated pools.
- Any private offer >$150k will route to our sales leadership + finance for approval; typical internal approvers: AM -> Sales Manager -> Finance Director -> Legal for terms/PO review.
- Co-sell credits do not change the buyer invoice in AWS private offers; they affect our internal partner crediting and occasionally require an additional seller form for AP reconciliation.

Details / options:
1) Yearly committed private offer (recommended for predictable spend)
   - Structure: Customer commits $X/year; we provision dedicated capacity or a commit-backed hosted tier. AWS PO shows the agreed pricing and term.
   - Discounting: For a 12-month commit at scale (>$200k/year) we typically start at ~15% off hosted rate; for larger commits we can increase to ~25–30% with standard SLA add-ons.
   - Approvals: Because it’s a contractual commitment on our side, we need AM sign-off, finance acceptance of billing cadence, and legal review of any special term exceptions (data retention, termination rights).

2) Usage-first private offer (recommended for exploratory / variable usage)
   - Structure: Buyer uses the private offer listing with the usage meter; no financial commit beyond buyer's PO terms.
   - Pricing: Closer to hosted on-demand; smaller volume discounts may apply via marketplace pricing tiers. Easier procurement since there's no long-term seller liability.

3) Term length tradeoffs
   - 12-month: predictable, best price/perf; requires internal approvals and sometimes a PO cadence (annual vs monthly billing).
   - 24–36 month: possible if buyer wants deeper discounts, but expect additional legal review and potentially custom SLA/termination clauses.

4) Approvals & timelines
   - For private offers that require Finance/CFO approval on the buyer side, we usually allow a two-week review window. On our side, internal approvals typically take 3–7 business days for standard discounts and 10–15 days for larger exceptions.

5) Co-sell and marketplace mechanics
   - Co-sell does not change the private offer invoice to the buyer. If Clearwave wants Redwood+AWS co-sell engagement, we’ll coordinate with our GTM partner lead; AWS may require an internal request and seller form to enable co-sell credits. That paperwork lives on the AWS partner console — we’ll handle it, but it slightly increases time-to-close (~3 business days extra).

Next step: Vanessa / Marcus — can you review the attached PDF I prepared with two price/term scenarios (committed 12m vs usage) and confirm internal approval lane & expected turnaround? Aisha — I’ll set a calendar for a 30m procurement sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Irene
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Looping in finance context and approval lane. Key notes for procurement:

- Thresholds: Confirm that $150k/year is the buyer's internal trigger. On Redwood side, discounts >20% or multi-year commitments route to Sales Director + Legal.
- Billing cadence preferences: We can invoice annually or monthly on net-30. For Clearwave we recommend annual invoicing to simplify accounting but we will accept monthly invoicing if that's a hard requirement.
- PO language: Standard AWS private offer PO is acceptable. If Clearwave inserts non-standard terms (data residency, indemnity expansion), Legal will need 7–10 business days to review.
- Finance checks: We’ll need a standard W-9/PO copy and a contact in Clearwave finance for ACH paperwork.

Action for sales: Irene/Marcus — if you plan to price at or below 15% off hosted, route through me for sign-off. If you go deeper (>20%) we’ll need to document an approval thread and capture that in HubSpot.

-Vanessa
VP, Revenue Operations

Quick product + GTM notes from my side:

- Dedicated vs hosted commit: If Clearwave wants predictable latency for peak hours across clinical shift changes, recommend Dedicated capacity. Commit sizes: $120k/year for a small dedicated pool (baseline), $300k/year for mid-tier throughput.
- For committed offers we include a token-based SKU and a throughput add-on; we can model both a flat annual commitment and a blended committed+overage structure (e.g., commit covers 80% of projected tokens, overage at a reduced on-demand rate).
- Co-sell: If Clearwave's AE wants joint customer-engagement with AWS, flag it now so we submit the co-sell nomination early. AWS approvals for co-sell credits are separate and do not modify buyer PO terms.

Pricing scenarios (rough, for negotiation):
A) 12-month committed (recommended) — $210k/year (15% off list), annual invoice, includes 5% reserved throughput buffer.
B) Usage-first private offer — estimated $260k/year at current projected usage, billed monthly via AWS meters, no seller liability on commit.

I'll prepare a short spreadsheet mapping their projected token usage to cost under A vs B so procurement can see break-even points.

-Marcus
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
